<action type="say">Here’s a concrete playbook you can follow if you get to the airport and see DL3391 is cancelled:

1. Get in **multiple queues at once**
   - Walk straight to the **Delta gate agent** for DL3391 (or the nearest Delta customer service desk) and **get in line**.
   - While you’re in line, if your phone starts behaving:
     - Go to **delta.com → My Trips / Check in / Flight Status** and look for a **“Change flight” or “Rebook”** button on your trip.
     - If you see Delta’s phone number posted at the gate, you can also **call from the line**.  
   - Goal: be working **app/site/phone + physical line** at the same time. Take whichever fixes it first.

2. Know your priorities before you speak to anyone
   Quickly decide:
   - **Earliest time you MUST arrive** at destination.
   - How flexible you are about:
     - Number of connections (1 vs 2),
     - Nearby airports (e.g., SFO/OAK, JFK/LGA/EWR–type situations),
     - Red‑eye / very early morning.
   Having this in your head lets you say “yes” fast to good options and not lose seats.

3. When you reach an agent, use this script
   - Start with:  
     “My flight DL3391 was just cancelled. I really need to get to [CITY] by [TIME] if at all possible. Can you please look at **any earlier or same‑day options**, including connections?”
   - Add if needed:  
     “I’m happy to connect or use a nearby airport as long as I can get in by [TIME].”

4. Grab **any solid seat**, then optimize
   - If they offer you **any confirmed seat today** that gets you in reasonably close to when you need: **take it immediately**.
   - After you’re confirmed, you can ask:  
     “Are there any earlier options you could also list me on **standby** for?”

5. Use standby + backup together
   - If only options are:
     - **Standby today** AND
     - **Confirmed tomorrow**  
     Say: “Please put me on standby for everything today **and** keep that confirmed seat for tomorrow as a backup.”
   - That way you have:
     - A **shot** at leaving today, and
     - A **guaranteed** seat if today doesn’t work out.

6. Ask what Delta will cover (so you’re not stuck)
   - If the cancellation is **Delta’s fault** (mechanical, crew, etc. – often the agent will hint at this):
     - Ask: “Since this was a Delta‑controlled cancellation, can you help with a **hotel** and **meal vouchers** if I have to overnight?”
   - If it’s **weather/ATC**, hotels are usually on you, but still ask:
     - “Do you have any **distress rates** at nearby hotels?” (discounts they can access).

7. Keep checking for better options
   - Even **after** you’re rebooked, occasionally refresh:
     - Delta site/app (once it loads later),
     - Or ask another agent if you see a clearly better flight with open seats.
   - Politely: “I’m currently on [NEW FLIGHT], but I see [OTHER FLIGHT]. Are there any seats you can move me to there?”

8. If you have checked bags
   - Tell the agent: “I have a checked bag from DL3391. Can you confirm it’s **retagged** to my new flight?”
   - If you end up **overnighting** without flying out:
     - Ask if you can **retrieve your bag** or if it must stay in the system.

If you later remember your origin/destination or have a must‑arrive time (e.g., “I have to be in X city by 10am Sunday”), tell me and I can suggest specific types of reroutes to ask Delta for, tailored to that route.</action>
